description: Hand-curated, corpus-grounded test set (authored directly from indexed chunks; regenerate candidates with eval/make_testset.py once a local LLM backend is available). Categories: code-lookup (hinges on a course code — BM25's job), multi-hop (spans chunks — the agent/reranker's job), collision (edition- or cohort-qualified — the corpus's trap), policy. gold_ids are valid ONLY for the 3,770-chunk index built 2026-08-31 from the full live-2627 + archive-2526 crawl; regenerate after any re-ingest.

items.question: What are the prerequisites for CPSC 221?
items.reference_answer: One of CPSC 210 or CPEN 221, and either one of CPSC 121, MATH 220 (or MATH_O 220), or a score of 68% or higher in MATH 226.

items.question: What are the prerequisites for CPSC 320?
items.reference_answer: CPSC 221 (or DSCI 221) plus at least 3 credits of MATH or STAT at the 200 level or above (the 2025/26 edition also accepted COMM 291 or BIOL 300 for the second part).

items.question: What are the prerequisites for CPSC 313?
items.reference_answer: CPSC 213, and either CPSC 221 or DSCI 221.

items.question: Which courses satisfy the prerequisite for MATH 200, Calculus III?
items.reference_answer: One of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121, SCIE 001, MATH_O 101, or MATH_O 103.

items.question: How many credits is CPSC 110 worth and what does it cover?
items.reference_answer: CPSC 110 (Computation, Programs, and Programming) is worth 4 credits and covers fundamental program and computation structures.

items.question: Compare the B.A. degree requirements for students who entered the program in 2023/24 with those who entered in 2024/25 or later.
items.reference_answer: Students entering 2023/24 or earlier must complete seven requirements: Writing and Research, Language, Science, Literature, Outside, Upper-level, and Arts Credit Minimum. Students entering 2024/25 or later complete five: Writing and Research, Ways of Knowing Breadth, Outside, Upper-level, and Arts Credit Minimum — the separate Language, Science, and Literature requirements are folded into the Ways of Knowing Breadth requirement.

items.question: How does admission to the Bachelor of Computer Science program differ from B.Sc. admission from secondary school?
items.reference_answer: Bachelor of Computer Science admission is a competitive selection process evaluating applicants on academic and other criteria (not every qualified applicant is admitted); B.Sc. admission from secondary school requires starting first year in September of the Winter session of admission (January starts are not permitted).

items.question: I have finished CPSC 210. What else do I need to complete before I can take CPSC 313?
items.reference_answer: CPSC 313 requires CPSC 213 and either CPSC 221 or DSCI 221. CPSC 221 in turn requires (beyond CPSC 210) one of CPSC 121, MATH 220, MATH_O 220, or a 68%+ score in MATH 226. So after CPSC 210 you still need CPSC 213 and CPSC 221 (with its discrete-math prerequisite).

items.question: In the 2025/26 calendar, what is the minimum number of credits required for a B.Sc. degree?
items.reference_answer: A minimum of 120 credits (a major, double major, or General Science option requires at least 120 credits but may require more).

items.question: According to the current 2026/27 calendar, what is the minimum number of credits required for a B.Sc. degree?
items.reference_answer: A minimum of 120 credits (a major, double major, or General Science option requires at least 120 credits but may require more).

items.question: Does a B.A. student who entered the program in 2024/25 or later have to complete a language requirement?
items.reference_answer: No. Their five degree requirements are Writing and Research, Ways of Knowing Breadth, Outside, Upper-level, and Arts Credit Minimum — there is no separate language requirement (that applies to students who entered in 2023/24 or earlier).

items.question: What are the three levels of academic standing at UBC?
items.reference_answer: In Good Standing; On Academic Probation; and Failed, Required to Withdraw. All students are In Good Standing on initial entry to the University.
